evidence: A rule sheet and its results, nothing in it validated: the framework is the sound section of the author's Terlunan reference (v0.6, section 2, outside the repository); each parent language's rules are choices made on 20 November 2026; the parent words are written from general knowledge of Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Mongolian, Quechua, Arabic, Tamazight, Swahili, Tagalog, Hebrew, Japanese and Esperanto, and no dictionary or speaker has checked them. No name is changed by this record: district_names.py and place_names.json stand as they are.
reading_rule: tongues gives, for every word of district_names.py's lexicons, its key, its role (head, modifier, or the word for an old name's meaning), the draft's spelling, the parent form it passes from (a code for the parent's rule sheet, a colon and the word in the parent's letters or the draft's), the form names are fused from (read), the word standing alone (passed), its syllables with the stressed one in capitals (said) and any fault against the framework; changed counts the words whose spelling moves, fallen_together lists pairs the draft kept apart and the pass makes one. pins gives every name in place_names.json with its passed form. record gives how many of the draft record's generated names the pass would change.

framework.stress: the syllable before the last, or the rightmost long vowel

rule_sheets.kk:
Kazakh and Kyrgyz in their own letters. Kept: ng, final consonants, the rounding harmony. Changed: the uvular
stop and fricative to k and g; sh and z to s; the j of жылан to y, the sound it answers to across the Turkic
languages; front rounded ö and ü to o and u.
rule_sheets.mn:
Mongolian in its own letters. Kept: long vowels, written double. Changed: its sibilants and affricates to s; a
final soft sign is the old -i (говь, gobi).
rule_sheets.qu:
Quechua in its standard spelling. Kept: the lowering of i and u to e and o beside the uvular q, which Quechua
speaks and does not write, so that qucha is kosa when q becomes k. Changed: q to k; ch and sh to s; ll and ñ to l
and n; the aspirated and ejective stops to the plain ones.
rule_sheets.ar:
Arabic and Tamazight in Latin letters, with ʿ and ʾ where the parent has them. Kept: the two throat stops as
the framework's glottal stop; f. Changed: the emphatics to their plain partners and q to k, as the reference does
with its Akkadian words; kh and the deep h to h; gh to g; sh, z and th to s, s and t; j to g, as Cairo says it;
long vowels to short.
rule_sheets.sw:
Swahili in its standard spelling; m° marks the syllabic m of the tree-and-river class. Kept: its five vowels,
which are the framework's; f and v; ng as the framework's ng. Changed: sh, ch and z to s; j to y; a syllabic nasal
gets back the vowel it lost, mu- in the tree-and-river class (mto, muto) and i- before the nasal elsewhere, as
its sister languages have it (mvua, imvua); a consonant and a glide that open a word get a vowel between.
rule_sheets.tl:
Tagalog in its standard spelling, with its glottal stop written where it stands between vowels. Tagalog's
sounds are the framework's own.
rule_sheets.he: Hebrew in Latin letters. Kept: f and v. Changed: sh, ts and z to s; kh and the deep h to h; q to k.
rule_sheets.ja:
Japanese in the Hepburn spelling. Kept: its five vowels and long vowels. Changed to the spelling that follows
its own sound system: shi, chi, tsu, fu are si, ti, tu, hu; z and j are s; a consonant and y before a vowel get
an i between (kyo, kiyo).
rule_sheets.eo:
The author's Esperanto-based tongue in its own spelling. Kept: f and v. Changed: j, its y sound, is written y;
the hatted ĥ and ŝ to h and s; ĝ to g; ĉ, ĵ, c and z to s.
rule_sheets.te:
Terlunan's words are the framework's own; a coined word still in its Māori spelling takes f for wh, as the
reference's fanga does.
rule_sheets.la: A name from elsewhere in Latin letters with its sounds marked (zh, sh, ch, ts, z, j, q, long vowels).

words.note: the draft's Zalam would read as the Arabic for peace once z is s; ʿatma is darkness
the throat stop between the two vowels of tsaʿar keeps them apart
the draft's Kparuparu was a slip for paruparu
the draft's kollar is the Uzbek plural; көлдөр is the Kyrgyz
the draft's tus (түс) would fall together with salt (тұз); арман is Kazakh for a dream or longing
the draft's umyt (ұмыт) would fall together with hope (үміт); унут is the Kyrgyz
